newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police say rebel chief's doctor arrested.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police say rebel chief's doctor arrested.

text.p: Sri Lankan police have arrested a man alleged to be the personal physician of the leader of the Tamil Tiger rebels, police said on Wednesday.
Police said the man was questioned about the medical services of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), including emergency units to treat its wounded fighters.
"The doctor is reported to have worked at a hospital run by the Tigers in Jaffna and several terrorist camps," a Crime Detective Bureau official said.
Police said they believed the man was the personal doctor of rebel chief Velupillai Prabhakaran, but they declined to reveal his name.
The man claimed he had come to Colombo to escape from the LTTE, police officials said, but they said they suspected he had another motive and were investigating.
The rebels are fighting a 13-year-old war against government troops for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The rebels say the number is higher.
